Changes in Long-Term Care Needs, Healthcare Costs, and Mortality Risk After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Japan: The Longevity Improvement & Fair Evidence Study.
items.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is increasingly performed in older adults with severe aortic stenosis, but there is limited evidence on their post-procedure changes in care needs, healthcare costs, and mortality risk. This retrospective cohort study used linked medical and long-term care (LTC) insurance claims data from 1361 patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent TAVI in 13 Japanese municipalities. Patients were stratified into four groups by baseline certified care needs level: Independent (n = 725), Support Level 1-2 (n = 321), LTC Level 1-2 (n = 208), and LTC Level 3-5 (n = 107). Among 532 patients in the 36-month observation cohort, 53% were independent at baseline, and approximately half of those remained independent at 36 months. Monthly total medical and LTC costs at 36 months were approximately 5 times higher in the LTC Level 3-5 group than the Independent group. The LTC Level 3-5 group also showed significantly higher all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 3.19, 95% confidence interval 2.18-4.67). Higher baseline care needs are associated with poorer outcomes and higher costs after TAVI. Incorporating care needs levels into clinical assessments may inform clinical decision-making and resource planning in older populations.

items.title: Management of Patients After Cardiac Arrest.
items.abstract: Cardiac arrest remains a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, although contemporary care now enables potential survival with good neurologic outcome. The core acute management goals for survivors of cardiac arrest are to provide organ support, sustain adequate hemodynamics, and evaluate the underlying cause of the cardiac arrest. In this article, the authors review the current state of knowledge and clinical intensive care unit practice recommendations for patients after cardiac arrest, particularly focusing on important areas of uncertainty, such as targeted temperature management, neuroprognostication, coronary evaluation, and hemodynamic targets.

items.title: Arrhythmias in Adult Congenital Heart Disease Heart Failure.
items.abstract: Heart failure and arrhythmias represent 2 major causes of mortality and morbidity in adults with congenital heart disease. Arrhythmias and heart failure are interdependent, and one may exacerbate the other. Treatment of one also has a positive impact on the other. Management approaches need to be multifaceted, including pharmacotherapy, optimization of hemodynamic status with catheter-based or surgical interventions, and specific management of arrhythmia with device or catheter ablation therapy.

items.title: DNA Immunotherapy (INO-3107) Long-Term Efficacy Supported by Enhanced Immunogenicity in HPV-6/11 RRP.
items.abstract: Recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), caused by chronic HPV-6/11 infection, leads to repeated papilloma growth requiring frequent surgical removal. DNA immunotherapy INO-3107 aims to induce HPV antigen-specific T-cell responses and reduce surgical burden. This analysis evaluated HPV-specific immune responses after INO-3107 and their association with long-term clinical outcomes. Adults with HPV-6/11-associated RRP received INO-3107 in a Phase 1/2 trial and were followed for one year, with additional clinical follow-up in a long-term extension. Number of surgeries in Years 1 and 2 was compared with the pre-treatment year. Blood and laryngotracheal tissue collected at Day 0 and Year 1 were analyzed for treatment-related changes in T-cell activity. Safety was assessed throughout. Thirty-two patients were treated; 28 continued into Year 2. At Year 1, most evaluable patients showed increased T-cell activity: 73% (19/26) demonstrated persistent expanded T-cell populations in blood, 71% (12/17) showed higher T-cell clone counts in laryngotracheal tissue, indicating site-specific immune infiltration. Antiviral T-cell signatures were enriched in 88% for CD4+ Th1 and CD8+ cytotoxic, and 71% for CD8+ effector memory, suggesting durable proinflammatory and memory responses in airway tissue. Mean annual surgeries decreased over time in the overall population (Baseline: 4.1, Year 1: 1.7, Year 2: 0.9). Similar durable reductions were observed in Responder subgroups. INO-3107 was well-tolerated, with no treatment-related serious adverse events. INO-3107 generates increased HPV-directed T-cell responses and substantially reduced surgical procedures over two years, supporting its ability to provide long-term clinical benefit in RRP without requiring additional surgeries during the dosing window.

Lemon extracellular vesicle-integrated in-situ hydrogel: A multifunctional platform for the synergistic treatment of breast cancer via chemotherapy, photodynamic therapy, and immunotherapy.
items.abstract: Combination therapy has attracted widespread attention in the field of cancer treatment. However, the complexity of the tumor microenvironment makes it difficult to achieve precise targeting and controlled drug release at the tumor site. Therefore, this study developed a multifunctional delivery system (LEVs-Gel@DOX/Ce6) that integrates combination therapy with smart controlled release: Lemon extracellular vesicles (LEVs) were used as the carrier scaffold to load doxorubicin (DOX) and dihydropyrrole e6 (Ce6) into nanoparticles, which were then dispersed in a smart hydrogel (Gel) composed of oxidized hyaluronic acid (OHA) and carboxymethyl chitosan (CMCs). Following intratumoral injection combined with 660 nm laser irradiation (Laser, +L), the system utilizes the hydrogel's local reservoir function to achieve prolonged drug retention while enabling precise, pH-responsive drug release. Through the synergistic effects of chemotherapy, photodynamic therapy, and immunotherapy, this system directly kills tumor cells by activating apoptosis and ferrocytosis pathways, induces immunogenic cell death (ICD) to stimulate an antitumor immune response, and simultaneously inhibits autophagolysosomal degradation and tumor cell proliferation. In vivo tumor suppression experiments showed that the system achieved a 92.32% inhibition rate against 4T1 breast cancer, delivering highly effective and low-toxicity therapeutic outcomes and providing a novel strategy for the precision treatment of breast cancer.

items.title: Acute-on-chronic liver failure: A global multisociety consensus on definitions.
items.abstract: The acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) multisociety harmonisation initiative represents a global collaborative effort to establish a unified, evidence-based framework for the definition, diagnosis, grading, and management of ACLF. Building on the strengths of existing regional definitions and integrating diverse international perspectives, this consensus provides a pragmatic, globally applicable foundation for clinical practice, research, and education. It also establishes a common framework for patient stratification, organ dysfunction and failure assessment, critical care management, liver transplantation, and the design of future phase II/III trials. Standardised, regulatory-aligned endpoints are expected to improve cross-study comparability, strengthen collaboration, and accelerate development of effective ACLF therapies.

items.title: The Prevalence of Occult Hepatitis B Virus Infection in Immunized Children Born to Mothers Who Are Hepatitis B Carriers.
items.abstract: Occult hepatitis B virus infection is characterized by the presence of hepatitis B virus DNA despite the undetectable hepatitis B surface antigen. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of occult hepatitis B virus infection in children born to hepatitis B surface antigen-positive mothers who received complete immunoprophylaxis. This cross-sectional study included 99 children. All received hepatitis B vaccination and hepatitis B immune globulin within 24 hours after birth. Serological markers and serum hepatitis B virus DNA were assessed in children aged 9 months to 15 years. All children were negative for hepatitis B surface antigen and serum hepatitis B virus DNA. The prevalence of serum-detectable occult hepatitis B virus infection was 0% (95% confidence interval: 0-3.6%). Anti-hepatitis B surface antibody seropositivity (≥ 10 IU/L) was observed in 66.7% of the children. Four children older than 24 months were positive for anti-hepatitis B core IgG antibody and anti-hepatitis B e antibody, possibly reflecting previous exposure without evidence of active infection. In these children, serum hepatitis B virus DNA remained negative at the initial assessment and at the 6- and 12-month follow-up assessments. No serum-detectable occult hepatitis B virus infection cases were identified. Complete immunoprophylaxis appears effective in this population; however, larger prospective studies with serial hepatitis B virus DNA testing are needed. Eine okkulte Hepatitis-B-Virusinfektion (OBI) ist durch das Vorhandensein von HBV-DNA bei nicht nachweisbarem HBsAg gekennzeichnet. Ziel dieser Studie war es, die Prävalenz der OBI bei Kindern zu ermitteln, die von HBsAg-positiven Müttern geboren wurden, die eine vollständige Immunprophylaxe erhalten hatten.An dieser Querschnittsstudie nahmen 99 Kinder teil. Alle erhielten innerhalb von 24 Stunden nach der Geburt eine Hepatitis-B-Impfung und HBIG. Serologische Marker und die HBV-DNA im Serum wurden bei Kindern im Alter von 9 Monaten bis 15 Jahren bestimmt.Alle Kinder waren negativ für HBsAg und HBV-DNA im Serum. Die Prävalenz einer im Serum nachweisbaren OBI betrug 0% (95%-KI: 0–3,6%). Bei 66,7% der Kinder wurde eine Anti-HBs-Seropositivität (≥ 10 IE/l) festgestellt. Vier Kinder, die älter als 24 Monate waren, waren positiv auf Anti-HBc-IgG und Anti-HBe, was möglicherweise auf eine frühere Exposition ohne Anzeichen einer aktiven Infektion hindeutet. Bei diesen Kindern blieb die HBV-DNA im Serum bei der Erstuntersuchung sowie bei den Nachuntersuchungen nach 6 und 12 Monaten negativ.Es wurden keine Fälle von OBI festgestellt, die im Serum nachweisbar waren. Eine vollständige Immunprophylaxe scheint bei dieser Population wirksam zu sein; es sind jedoch größere prospektive Studien mit serienmäßigen HBV-DNA-Tests erforderlich.

items.title: Long-Term Durability and Safety Signals of Systemic AAV Gene Therapy for Haemophilia A and B: A Systematic Review.
items.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy can provide sustained endogenous factor expression after a single infusion, but durability and safety differ across products. We synthesised long-term efficacy and clinically interpretable safety outcomes while avoiding inappropriate class-level pooling. Five databases were searched from inception to 15 May 2026 for prospective systemic AAV trials in haemophilia A or B. Overlapping reports were linked by trial identifier, vector/transgene, dose, enrolment, sites, sample size and follow-up. One additional eligible report published within the search window was identified during peer review and incorporated. The primary outcome was product-specific factor activity at the latest follow-up with clinical durability. Prophylaxis status, bleeding and safety were synthesised descriptively by product because baseline regimens, outcome definitions and observation windows were not sufficiently harmonised for cross-product pooling. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I. Fourteen unique cohorts were included: six in haemophilia A and eight in haemophilia B. Reported long-term factor activity remained product-specific. The GS001 Phase 1 study reported median FVIII activity of 5.6 IU/dL at Week 144 in the low-dose cohort and 42.7 IU/dL at Week 104 in the high-dose cohort. Prophylaxis and zero-treated-bleed outcomes were not pooled because baseline treatment, restart criteria, denominators and observation windows differed. Liver abnormalities, immunosuppressive exposure, treatment-related serious adverse events and loss of expression varied by product. Rare inhibitor and thrombotic events reported outside the eligible prospective cohort synthesis reinforce the need for ongoing product-specific surveillance. Selected patients experienced sustained haemostatic benefit, and several FIX programmes showed stable multiyear expression. Because assays, products, immune-management strategies and follow-up differed, counselling and surveillance should remain product-specific. Standardised longitudinal reporting is required for stronger comparative conclusions.

items.title: Brief report: Clinical and Functional Characterization of Rare Germline and Somatic EGFR Variants in Three Patients with Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
items.abstract: To date hereditary risk factors for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) are poorly understood. While most cases are considered sporadic, rare monogenic germline alterations in EGFR and TP53 have been reported to be associated with increased risk of NSCLC. While identification and accurate functional characterization of such variants are essential for improving risk assessment and personalized therapeutic strategies, they remain limited. Germline whole genome sequencing (WGS) was performed to identify potential hereditary causes of NSCLC within Task Force 5 of the German National Network for Genomic Medicine. Detected EGFR variants were further investigated using in silico structural modeling and in vitro functional characterization in Ba/F3 cell models to investigate their oncogenic potential and sensitivity to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs). We identified two different EGFR germline variants (NM_005228.5:c.2155G>A, p.(Gly719Ser); NM_005228.5: c.2327G>A, p.(Arg776His)) in three patients with NSCLC, each harboring a different somatic compound variants (p.(Gly719Ser)+p.(Ser768Ile), p.(Gly719Ala)+p.(Arg776His), p.(Arg776His)+p.(Leu861Gln) (liver metastasis) and p.(Arg776His)+p.(Gly719Ser)). In silico analyses predict that p.(Gly719Ser) and p.(Gly719Ala) stabilize the active EGFR kinase conformation, whereas p.(Ser768Ile), p.(Arg776His) and p.(Leu861Gln) destabilize the inactive conformation. Consistent with these predictions, cis co-expression of the compound variants in the Ba/F3 assay demonstrated oncogenic activity and sensitivity to afatinib. Clinically two individuals achieved a partial response to afatinib treatment. These findings highlight the clinical relevance of germline EGFR variants in NSCLC and support the value of in-silico and in-vitro analyses for variant interpretation and response prediction. Broadening germline testing and functional variant characterization may enhance risk prediction and targeted therapy for individuals with NSCLC.

items.title: ROS-responsive supramolecular hydrogel system for the controlled release of oncolytic adenovirus and paclitaxel in cancer therapy.
items.abstract: The synergistic combination of oncolytic adenovirus (oAd) and paclitaxel chemodrug holds great potential for cancer therapy as it can enhance cell apoptosis, the viral replication in cancer cells, and induce a potent antitumor effect. However, clinical output is insufficient because of the rapid blood clearance and inactivation of viral activity within high-reactive oxygen species (ROS) tumor microenvironment (TME). In this regard, we have developed an ROS responsive supramolecular hydrogel (mPEG-b-PCL-DPMP/α-cyclodextrin (DPMP/α-CD hydrogel)) system to protect oAd bioactivity while providing sustained, localized co-delivery of paclitaxel (PTX). The amount of ROS was evaluated by fluorescence measurements using H 2 DCFDA as a probe and confirmed that there was a significant decrease in ROS level by DPMP/α-CD hydrogel. An in vivo degradation study showed that the hydrogel underwent substantial degradation within one week. Furthermore, oAd and PTX encapsulated in DPMP/α-CD hydrogel were released consistently and retained the viral activity, exhibiting cancer cell killing efficacy under strong tumor microenvironment conditions. In vivo, a single intratumoral injection formed a stable depot that persisted for over a week, leading to superior tumor regression in H460 xenograft models compared to naked oAd or PTX alone. Histological and biochemical analyses confirmed no detectable histopathological abnormalities in the examined major organs or elevations in the measured serum liver and kidney injury markers under the conditions evaluated. Altogether, this ROS-responsive shield-and-release injectable supramolecular hydrogel platform loaded with oAd/PTX exhibits downregulated ROS level at tumor microenvironment and enhanced anti-tumor effect. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: • An active shield-scavenge-release hydrogel was engineered to enhance oncolytic adenovirus/paclitaxel (oAd/PTX) combination therapy. • The hydrogel protects oxidation-sensitive adenovirus while enabling sustained local viral release. • ROS-responsive dipentaerythritol hexakis(3-mercaptopropionate) (DPMP) segments convert the oxidative tumor microenvironment into a therapeutic release trigger. • PTX-loaded hydrophobic domains support prolonged chemotherapy without disrupting hydrogel architecture. • Sustained oAd/PTX co-release amplifies viral replication, tumor cell killing, and antitumor efficacy. • A single intratumoral administration achieves durable tumor suppression with minimal systemic toxicity.

items.title: Comparative cytogenotoxicity of benzo[b]fluoranthene and benzo[ghi]perylene and their binary mixture in human peripheral blood, lung (A549), and liver (HepG2) cells.
items.abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) occur in complex mixtures, yet their comparative cytogenotoxic effects remain insufficiently characterized. We investigated benzo[b]fluoranthene (BbF), benzo[ghi]perylene (BghiP), and their binary mixture in human blood-derived models, A549, and HepG2 cells. Viability was assessed using fluorescent dual staining or MTT, while genotoxicity was evaluated using alkaline comet and cytokinesis-block micronucleus assays. BbF reduced blood-cell viability across a broader concentration range than BghiP, whereas A549 cells showed minimal cytotoxic responses. HepG2 cells exhibited concentration- and time-dependent viability reductions and significant DNA damage after 24h of individual and binary exposure. Binary exposure increased nuclear buds in A549 cells and nucleoplasmic bridges in HepG2 cells; micronucleus frequencies increased without consistently reaching statistical significance. Responses varied across models and endpoints under controlled in vitro conditions. These findings support further investigation of co-occurring PAHs, although additivity, synergism, and antagonism were not evaluated.

items.title: Chronic Alcohol Consumption Expands Bone Marrow Myelopoiesis While Suppressing Splenic Hematopoiesis.
items.abstract: Chronic alcohol consumption-mediated immune dysregulation elevates the risk of multiple diseases, yet how these immunological alterations manifest across tissues remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the impact of chronic alcohol consumption on hematopoiesis and immune homeostasis across the bone marrow (BM), spleen (SP), and peripheral blood (PB) using female C57BL/6 mice fed a Lieber-DeCarli liquid diet with 6% (v/v) ethanol for 6 weeks. Alcohol consumption induced a mild hepatic injury, evidenced by increased liver weight, elevated plasma levels of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and hepatic steatosis without fibrosis. Immune phenotyping by high-dimensional spectral flow cytometry showed that, in the BM, alcohol expanded myeloid-biased multipotent progenitors 2 and 3 (MPP2 and MPP3), granulocyte-monocyte progenitors (GMPs), and macrophages. Conversely, the SP exhibited reduced abundance and proliferative activity of lineage-negative c-KIT-positive (LK) and megakaryocyte-erythroid progenitor (MEP) populations, resulting in impaired erythropoiesis. Despite these tissue-specific alterations, PB exhibited comparatively subtle and more variable changes than the BM and SP. These findings demonstrate that alcohol-mediated hematopoietic remodeling is tissue-specific and may not be fully captured by PB analyses. They further highlight the potential need for improved tissue-informed biomarkers and diagnostic approaches to detect and monitor alcohol-mediated immune remodeling beyond PB.
